categories.name: Around the house
categories.blurb: The everyday work that keeps a home safe and working properly.

items.title: Switchboard upgrades
items.blurb: Ceramic fuses and old boards replaced with a modern enclosure, RCBOs on every circuit and room to grow. Usually a day's work.

items.title: Safety switches (RCDs)
items.blurb: Queensland homes need them on power and lighting circuits. If yours only covers the power points, half your house is unprotected.

items.title: Lighting and LED upgrades
items.blurb: Downlight replacements, feature and outdoor lighting, dimming that actually works with the fittings you chose.

items.title: Power points and USB outlets
items.blurb: New outlets, relocations, weatherproof externals, and the double-with-USB everyone asks for in the kitchen.

items.title: Ceiling fans
items.blurb: Supply and install, or fit the one you've already bought. Includes wall control and existing point check.

items.title: Fault finding
items.blurb: Breakers that trip, lights that flicker, a circuit that's dead. We trace it properly rather than guessing and replacing parts.

categories.name: Renovations & rewires
categories.blurb: Working alongside builders, architects and owners on jobs that need planning, not just a spanner.

items.title: Full and partial rewires
items.blurb: Old rubber or cloth-insulated wiring replaced throughout. We stage it so you can stay living in the house wherever possible.

items.title: Renovation rough-in and fit-off
items.blurb: Planned with your builder from the frame stage. Every point marked up and agreed before a cable is pulled.

items.title: Lighting design
items.blurb: Layouts, circuit grouping and switching planned room by room. Far cheaper to think about before the plasterboard goes on.
items.priceNote: design fee, credited to the job

items.title: Kitchen and bathroom fit-outs
items.blurb: Appliance circuits, rangehoods, heated towel rails, exhaust fans, and the dedicated circuits induction cooktops need.

items.title: Data, TV and network
items.blurb: Cat6 runs, wall plates, TV points and patch panels — done at rough-in when it costs a fraction of retrofitting.

categories.name: Solar & EV
categories.blurb: The newer end of the trade, done by people who've actually been trained on it.

items.title: EV charger installation
items.blurb: 7kW single phase or 22kW three phase, load-tested against your existing supply so you don't trip the main when the car and the oven run together.

items.title: Switchboard preparation for solar
items.blurb: Most older boards need work before an inverter can be connected. We do that part properly so your solar installer isn't improvising.

items.title: Battery and inverter connection
items.blurb: Grid connection paperwork, isolation, and the metering changes Energex needs before anything is switched on.

items.title: Solar fault finding
items.blurb: System underperforming, inverter throwing errors, or export not showing on your bill. We test the electrical side independently of the installer.

categories.name: Commercial
categories.blurb: Shops, cafés, offices and body corporate work across the inner east.

items.title: Shop and café fit-outs
items.blurb: Three phase, equipment circuits, emergency and exit lighting, and the certification your council inspection will ask for.

items.title: Test and tag
items.blurb: Scheduled appliance testing with a register you can actually hand to an auditor. Priced per item, cheaper in volume.

items.title: Emergency and exit lighting
items.blurb: Installation plus the six-monthly discharge testing AS 2293 requires, logged and certified.

items.title: Thermal imaging
items.blurb: Switchboard scans that find failing connections before they fail. Insurers increasingly ask for these on commercial premises.

faq.q: Do I get a certificate when the work is done?
faq.a: Yes, always. Queensland law requires a Certificate of Testing for electrical work, and we issue one on every job without being asked. Keep it — you'll need it when you sell, and your insurer may ask for it after any incident.

faq.q: How much does a switchboard upgrade actually cost?
faq.a: Most single phase domestic upgrades land between $1,450 and $2,400 depending on the number of circuits, whether the main switch and meter need work, and whether there's asbestos backing behind the old board. We give a fixed price after seeing it, not a range.

faq.q: Can you work with my builder or do I need to organise everything?
faq.a: We work directly with builders and project managers on most renovation jobs. Give them our number and we'll deal with scheduling, rough-in timing and inspections. You only get involved for decisions that are actually yours to make, like where the lights go.

faq.q: Is an emergency callout worth it, or should I wait until morning?
faq.a: Call us and we'll tell you honestly, at no charge. Burning smells, visible arcing, water in a switchboard or a hot power point are genuine emergencies — turn the power off at the main switch and ring. A single dead circuit with no other symptoms can usually wait.

Not for standard domestic work. Larger renovation and commercial jobs that need a detailed take-off may carry a design fee, which we credit back against the job if you go ahead. We'll tell you before we start, never after.
Brisbane's inner east, roughly everything within fifteen minutes of Bulimba. We'll travel further for larger jobs — ask and we'll tell you straight away whether it makes sense.
